questions.prompt: Explain the difference between ModelContainer and ModelContext in SwiftData. Answer in 2–5 sentences.

rubric.criterion: Explains that ModelContainer manages physical storage, schema configuration, and migrations on disk
Explains that ModelContext acts as an in-memory scratchpad tracking mutations, inserts, deletes, and saves

questions.modelAnswer: ModelContainer manages the database schema and coordinates physical storage files such as SQLite on disk. In contrast, ModelContext serves as an in-memory workspace that tracks active changes, inserts, and deletions. Multiple contexts can operate simultaneously while backed by a single container.

questions.prompt: Explain how the @Query property wrapper operates in SwiftUI views. Answer in 2–5 sentences.

rubric.criterion: Explains that @Query fetches data directly from the ambient model context in the SwiftUI environment
States that @Query observes database changes and automatically refreshes the SwiftUI view

questions.modelAnswer: The @Query property wrapper fetches persistent models from the ambient ModelContext supplied by the SwiftUI environment. It automatically observes changes in the underlying database storage. When models are inserted, deleted, or modified, @Query triggers view updates to refresh the user interface.

questions.prompt: Why can you not pass a @Model instance directly into a background Task or actor, and what should you pass instead? Answer in 2–5 sentences.

rubric.criterion: Identifies that @Model instances are non-Sendable reference types bound to their specific context, creating data races if shared across threads
Explains that developers should pass PersistentIdentifier instead and fetch the object inside the target context or ModelActor

questions.modelAnswer: SwiftData models are non-Sendable reference types that are tied to their specific ModelContext. Passing them across concurrency boundaries causes compiler errors in Swift 6 and risks data races. Developers should pass the model PersistentIdentifier instead and fetch a local instance inside the background actor context.

questions.prompt: How does SwiftData handle relationships between models and how do cascade delete rules work? Answer in 2–5 sentences.

rubric.criterion: Explains how models declare relationships to other model instances or collections
Explains that cascade delete automatically removes related child models when the parent model is deleted

questions.modelAnswer: SwiftData models define relationships by referencing other @Model classes directly or within collections. Using the @Relationship(deleteRule: .cascade) attribute tells the framework to delete all associated child models when the parent entity is removed. This prevents orphaned records from remaining in SQLite storage.

questions.modelAnswer: You configure an in-memory container by initializing a ModelConfiguration with isStoredInMemoryOnly set to true, then passing it to ModelContainer. This avoids creating persistent SQLite files on disk during execution. It ensures tests and SwiftUI previews start with clean state without polluting the file system.
